---
title: "Verification"
---

Agents produce plausible code. Verification is the part of the workflow that is yours,
and it is short enough to do every single time.

## The four-step minimum

1. **Read the diff.** `git diff` before you commit, or the diff in the pull request.
   If you cannot explain a change, do not merge it.
2. **Check the coding against the codebook.** Open the PDF. Confirm the response
   options, the missing-data codes, and the direction of the scale.
3. **Report `n_obs` and `n_miss`.** Every model, every time. If the N moved and nobody
   said why, cases were silently dropped.
4. **Write the test.** A check you run once is a check you will stop running.

## Reporting N

```r
voters <- wss |> filter(!is.na(trump_vote))
cat("n_obs =", nrow(voters),
    "| n_miss =", nrow(wss) - nrow(voters), "\n")

fit <- glm(trump_vote ~ latino * year, family = quasibinomial,
           weights = weight, data = voters)
cat("n_obs =", nobs(fit), "| n_miss =", nrow(voters) - nobs(fit), "\n")
```

The second pair matters most: listwise deletion inside a model formula is the most
common way a sample shrinks without anyone noticing.

## Turning a check into a test

Tests live in `tests/testthat/` and run with:

```bash
Rscript -e 'testthat::test_dir("tests/testthat")'
```

```r
test_that("authoritarianism is a 0-1 mean of four items", {
  wss <- readRDS("data/wss_clean.rds")
  expect_true(all(wss$authoritarianism >= 0 &
                  wss$authoritarianism <= 1, na.rm = TRUE))
})

test_that("trump_vote is coded only for two-party voters", {
  wss <- readRDS("data/wss_clean.rds")
  expect_setequal(unique(na.omit(wss$trump_vote)), c(0, 1))
})
```

::: {.note}
[A good use of an agent]{.note-head}
*"Read `R/01_recode.R` and write a `testthat` test for every derived variable: range,
allowed values, and row count. Do not change the recode."* Then read the tests — they
are far easier to check than the recode itself, and they will outlive this workshop.
:::

## Checking an agent's factual claims

| Claim it makes | How you check it |
|---|---|
| "`pid7` runs 1–7 with 4 as independent" | The codebook, not the data's range |
| "I dropped non-voters" | `n_miss`, and `count()` on the raw variable |
| "This uses survey weights" | Read the call. Look for `weights =` |
| "The 2024 weight is `weight`" | It is `weight_all`. See `AGENTS.md` |
| "Smith (2019) shows…" | Search for the citation. Assume it is invented |

::: {.warn}
[Reproducibility is the real test]{.warn-head}
Delete `data/wss_clean.rds` and `output/`, then run the pipeline from the top. If the
numbers come back identical, the work is reproducible. If they do not, something lives
in a console somewhere instead of in a script.
:::

## What to trust

- **Trust** code you have read and can explain.
- **Trust** numbers that a script regenerates from raw data.
- **Do not trust** a result that exists only in a chat transcript.
- **Do not trust** your own memory of what you accepted ten minutes ago. That is what
  the commit history is for.
